bug_description.original: Crash Type: Stack-buffer-overflow READ 4 Crash State: Mat_VarReadNextInfo5 Mat_GetDir MatioRead
bug_description.normalized: In Mat_VarReadNextInfo5, compressed MATLAB variable dimension data is decompressed into a fixed-size stack buffer uncomp_buf[16]. When InflateRankDims returns early (e.g., due to zlib stream termination after decompressing the tag) without allocating a heap buffer for dimensions, the dims pointer aliases the stack buffer at uncomp_buf+2. The rank derived from the decompressed tag byte count is not validated against the 14-element capacity of this alias. A crafted file with a dimension byte count exceeding 52 causes the dimension copy loop to read past the end of the stack buffer.

source.description: InflateRankDims decompresses attacker-controlled compressed data from the MAT file into the stack buffer uncomp_buf. The decompressed tag at uncomp_buf[0..1] holds the dimensions byte count, which is the vulnerability-relevant tainted value. If the zlib stream ends or errors during tag inflation, InflateRankDims returns early without allocating a heap dims buffer, leaving *dims NULL.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled zlib-compressed data in MAT5 file; decompressed tag byte count in uncomp_buf[1] controls the dimension rank.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: The copy loop reads dims[j] where dims aliases uncomp_buf+2. When j+2 >= 16 (rank > 13), dims[j] reads past the 16-element uncomp_buf stack array boundary, causing a 4-byte stack-buffer-overflow READ.

root_cause.description: The dimension rank is derived from the attacker-controlled decompressed byte count without validating that it fits within the stack buffer capacity when dims aliases uncomp_buf+2. The fix adds: if (0 == do_clean && matvar->rank > 13) { error; break; }.

parser_admitted.description: After InflateVarTag succeeds and uncomp_buf[0] == MAT_T_MATRIX, compressed variable parsing proceeds to array flags and rank/dimensions.

tainted_value_origin.description: The decompressed rank byte count in uncomp_buf[1] originates from attacker-controlled zlib-compressed data in the MAT5 file.

fine_trace.note: Inflates compressed data from MAT file into stack buffer uncomp_buf[16] (64 bytes). The decompressed tag writes uncomp_buf[0] (type) and uncomp_buf[1] (byte count). When the zlib stream ends or errors after tag inflation but before dimension processing, InflateRankDims returns early without setting *dims to a heap buffer, so *dims remains NULL. uncomp_buf[1] now holds the attacker-controlled rank byte count.
Since InflateRankDims left *dims as NULL, the dims pointer is aliased to uncomp_buf+2. This pointer can safely access at most 14 uint32_t elements (uncomp_buf[2] through uncomp_buf[15]).
The attacker-controlled decompressed byte count from uncomp_buf[1] is assigned to nbytes. For the PoC, this value exceeds 52 (e.g., 60), indicating more dimensions than the stack buffer can hold.

Rank is computed as byte count divided by sizeof(uint32_t). For nbytes=60, rank=15, exceeding the 14-element accessible range of dims (uncomp_buf+2). No bounds check validates rank against the stack buffer capacity.

Missing guard: no check that rank <= 13 when do_clean == 0 (dims aliases the stack buffer). The fix inserts: if (0 == do_clean && matvar->rank > 13) break. Without it, rank values derived from attacker-controlled data pass unchecked to the copy loop.

Loop iterates j=0..rank-1 reading dims[j]=uncomp_buf[j+2]. At j=14 (rank>=15), uncomp_buf[16] is accessed: 4 bytes past the 64-byte stack array boundary. ASAN reports stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at the end of uncomp_buf (stack offset 128, uncomp_buf occupies [64,128)).

format.name: MAT5
format.contract: A MAT5-format file containing a MAT_T_COMPRESSED data element whose zlib-compressed payload decompresses to a valid MAT_T_MATRIX variable tag and array flags, followed by a rank/dimensions tag with a byte count exceeding 52 (producing rank > 13). The compressed stream must terminate or error after the rank/dimensions tag inflation so that InflateRankDims returns without allocating a heap dims buffer, causing the caller to use the fixed-size stack buffer uncomp_buf[16] with an out-of-bounds rank.
